easy.prompt: Two fair six-sided dice are rolled. What is the probability of rolling a sum of 7?
easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: There are 36 equally-likely outcomes; six of them sum to 7: (1,6),(2,5),(3,4),(4,3),(5,2),(6,1). So 6/36 = 1/6.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: There are six outcomes summing to 7, not seven.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: That's the probability of a single specific pair like (1,6).
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Half of the correct answer — this misses three of the six outcomes.

easy.prompt: If P(A) = 1/2 and P(B|A) = 1/3, what is P(A ∩ B)?
easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: That's P(B|A) — the conditional, not the joint.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Not derivable from the given numbers.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: That's roughly P(A) + P(B|A), which isn't a valid formula.

easy.prompt: Events A and B are independent if and only if…
easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Independence is defined by factorization of the joint; equivalent forms: P(A|B) = P(A) when P(B) > 0.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: That says A and B can't co-occur — also mutual exclusivity.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Equal probabilities don't imply independence.

easy.prompt: A Bernoulli random variable with parameter p has expected value…
easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: That's the variance of a Bernoulli.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: That's E[X] for a Geometric distribution.

easy.prompt: If X ~ Binomial(n, p), what is E[X]?
easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: A Binomial is the sum of n independent Bernoulli(p)'s, so E[X] = np.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: That's the variance of a Binomial.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Not a standard quantity.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: That's E[X] for a single Bernoulli.

easy.prompt: Linearity of expectation says E[X + Y] equals E[X] + E[Y]…

choices.label: B
choices.body: Always, even when X and Y are dependent.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Only when X and Y have the same distribution.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Only when X and Y are independent.

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Linearity holds regardless of dependence — a key reason it's so useful.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: It holds for continuous too.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Independence is required for variance, not expectation.

easy.prompt: Var(X + Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y) holds when…

choices.label: A
choices.body: X and Y are identically distributed.

choices.label: B
choices.body: X and Y have the same mean.

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Var(X+Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y) + 2 Cov(X, Y); the cross term vanishes when correlation is zero.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Same distribution doesn't imply independence.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Means don't affect the variance identity.

easy.prompt: What is the probability of exactly k successes in n independent trials with success probability p?
easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: That's the Binomial probability mass function.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Not a probability at all.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Off — needs p^k and the failure term.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Missing the combinatorial coefficient and the failure factor.

easy.prompt: Bayes' theorem expresses P(A | B) as…
easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Bayes rewrites the conditional via the symmetry P(A ∩ B) = P(A|B)P(B) = P(B|A)P(A).

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Circular — that just gives P(A ∩ B).
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Not a probability formula.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: That's the joint when A, B are independent — not Bayes.

easy.prompt: If A and B are mutually exclusive, then P(A ∪ B) equals…
easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Disjoint events can't co-occur, so the inclusion-exclusion term P(A ∩ B) is zero.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Only true in degenerate cases.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Inclusion-exclusion with independence assumption — not for disjoint events.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: That's the joint under independence — not the union.

easy.prompt: The Poisson distribution with rate λ has mean…
easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: E[X] = Σ k · e^{−λ} λ^k / k! = λ; the Poisson is also its own variance.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: That's the mean of an Exponential.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Not a Poisson moment.

easy.prompt: If X is Exponential(λ), what is E[X]?
easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: The exponential pdf f(x) = λe^{−λx} integrates with x to give 1/λ.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: That's the rate parameter, not the mean.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Not a standard quantity.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Not a moment of the Exponential.

easy.prompt: Drawing one card from a standard 52-card deck, what is the expected value of its rank if A = 1, J = 11, Q = 12, K = 13?
easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Average of 1 through 13 is (1+13)/2 = 7; each rank has equal probability.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Off by one.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Off by one in the other direction.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: That's the mean of 1..12 — wrong upper bound.

easy.prompt: Three coins are flipped. What is the probability of exactly two heads?
easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Three outcomes out of eight have exactly two heads: HHT, HTH, THH.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: That's the probability of any head appearing once or more (excluding all-tails would be 7/8).
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: That's two specific outcomes, not three.

easy.prompt: A test has 99% sensitivity and 95% specificity for a disease with 1% prevalence. If a random person tests positive, the chance they actually have the disease is closest to…
easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Confusing test specificity with posterior probability.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Confusing sensitivity with posterior probability — base-rate fallacy.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: That's the prior, before conditioning on the positive test.

easy.prompt: A continuous uniform distribution on [a, b] has variance…
easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: By integration, σ² = (b − a)² / 12; the mean is (a+b)/2.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Off by a factor of 2.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Half the range, not a variance.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: That's the mean.

easy.prompt: The variance of a Bernoulli(p) random variable is…
easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Var = E[X²] − E[X]² = p − p² = p(1 − p).

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Off — missing the (1 − p) factor.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: That's the failure probability, not the variance.

easy.prompt: If X ~ Geometric(p) (number of trials until the first success), then E[X] is…
easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: By the formula for the geometric mean, on average you need 1/p trials.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: That's the success probability per trial.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Not a moment of the geometric.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: That's the mean of a Geometric counting failures, off by convention.

easy.prompt: An event A satisfies P(A) = 0.3. What is P(A^c) (the complement)?
easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Only if A is certain.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Only if A is impossible.

easy.prompt: If E[X] = 5 and Y = 3X + 2, what is E[Y]?
easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Linearity: E[3X + 2] = 3 E[X] + 2 = 15 + 2.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: That's E[X], not E[Y].
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Off by 4 — arithmetic error.

medium.prompt: If Var(X) = 4 and Y = 5X + 7, what is Var(Y)?
medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Var(aX + b) = a² Var(X) = 25 · 4. Constants don't change variance.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Added the constant; constants don't affect variance.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Mixed up — would result from incorrect formula.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Used a, not a², for the scaling.

medium.prompt: The standard normal has CDF Φ. P(−1.96 ≤ Z ≤ 1.96) is approximately…
medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: 1.96 standard deviations from the mean covers about 95% of a standard normal.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: That's the one-sigma range (±1).
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: That's roughly the ±2.58 range.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: That would be P(Z > 0) or P(Z < 0).

medium.prompt: The Central Limit Theorem states that, given i.i.d. random variables with finite variance, the standardized sample mean converges in distribution to…
medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Regardless of the underlying distribution (with finite mean and variance), the sample mean is asymptotically normal.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Only true for samples drawn from a normal.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: The CLT specifically gives the normal.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Cauchy has no finite variance; CLT doesn't apply there.

medium.prompt: If X and Y are independent Normal(μ_X, σ_X²) and Normal(μ_Y, σ_Y²), then X + Y is…
medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Means add, variances (not standard deviations) add when the variables are independent.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Variances add — standard deviations do not add directly.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Products of normals aren't normal in general.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Sum of independent normals is normal.

medium.prompt: P(A | B) = P(A) implies A and B are independent. What's another equivalent condition?
medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Independence is symmetric: knowing A doesn't change P(B) iff knowing B doesn't change P(A).

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: That's mutual exclusivity — typically incompatible with independence unless one has probability 0.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Covering the sample space isn't independence.

medium.prompt: If X ~ Geometric(p) counting trials until first success, P(X > k) equals…
medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: X > k means the first k trials are all failures, each with probability (1 − p).

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Not the survival function for Geometric.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: That's k successes in a row.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Not a probability.

medium.prompt: Cov(X, X) equals…
medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Cov(X, Y) = E[(X−μ_X)(Y−μ_Y)]; with Y = X this is Var(X).

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Only true for independent X, Y.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Only true for the correlation of X with itself.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Off by a factor.

medium.prompt: The Poisson approximates the Binomial(n, p) well when…

choices.label: A
choices.body: n is large and p is small with np = λ moderate.

choices.label: C
choices.body: n and p are both around 0.5.

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Poisson(np) is the limiting distribution as n → ∞, p → 0 with np fixed.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: The approximation is asymptotic in n.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Symmetric to the relevant regime but the Poisson approximates rare events.

medium.prompt: If X is uniform on {1, 2, …, n}, what is E[X²]?
medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Not the right closed form.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Not a standard moment.

medium.prompt: A discrete-time Markov chain is specified by…

choices.label: A
choices.body: A transition matrix P with P_{ij} = P(X_{t+1} = j | X_t = i).

choices.label: D
choices.body: A sequence of i.i.d. random variables.

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Together with an initial distribution π_0, the transition matrix fully determines the chain.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Rewards are an MDP concept; not needed for a chain.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Markov chains have dependence by definition.

medium.prompt: A stationary distribution π of a Markov chain satisfies…

choices.label: C
choices.body: πP = π (a left eigenvector with eigenvalue 1).

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Stationarity means the distribution is preserved after one step: π_j = Σ_i π_i P_{ij}.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Only stationary if state 1 absorbs.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Wrong direction — π should be a row vector multiplied on the left.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Probabilities can't all be zero.

medium.prompt: If X is a continuous random variable with density f and Y = g(X) for a strictly increasing differentiable g, the density of Y is…
medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Change-of-variables for densities; the Jacobian factor accounts for the stretching of probability mass.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Multiplied instead of divided by the derivative — wrong direction.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Ignores g entirely.

medium.prompt: Markov's inequality states that for a non-negative random variable X and a > 0…
medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: A general but often loose inequality; sharper variants (Chebyshev, Chernoff) use more information about X.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Reversed direction.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: It's an inequality, not equality, in general.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Wrong direction on the inequality.

medium.prompt: Chebyshev's inequality bounds P(|X − μ| ≥ kσ) by…
medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: For any distribution with mean μ and variance σ², the chance of being k stdev from the mean is at most 1/k².

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: That's a Chernoff-style bound, needing MGF assumptions.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Off — Chebyshev is in 1/k², which is tighter for large k.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Not a probability bound.

medium.prompt: Two events A, B with P(A) > 0 satisfy P(A | B) > P(A) iff…

choices.label: A
choices.body: P(B | A) > P(B), i.e., A and B are positively associated.

choices.label: D
choices.body: B is a subset of A.

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: By Bayes, P(A|B)/P(A) = P(B|A)/P(B); they exceed 1 together.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Mutual exclusivity would force P(A | B) = 0.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Magnitudes aren't what positive association is about.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: That gives P(A | B) = 1 ≥ P(A), but isn't the iff.

medium.prompt: The moment generating function (MGF) of a random variable X is…

choices.label: B
choices.body: Var(X) as a function of t.

choices.label: D
choices.body: M_X(t) = E[e^{tX}], when the expectation exists in a neighborhood of 0.

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: The MGF, when it exists, encodes all moments via derivatives at 0: M^{(n)}(0) = E[X^n].

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Characteristic functions use i (imaginary unit) and always exist; MGF uses real t.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Not how MGF is defined.

medium.prompt: A state i is absorbing in a Markov chain when…

choices.label: A
choices.body: P_{ii} = 1 (the chain stays in i forever once entered).

choices.label: B
choices.body: i is the most probable initial state.

choices.label: D
choices.body: P_{ij} = 0 for all j ≠ i and P_{ii} = 0.

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Absorbing states have a self-loop probability of 1.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Initial distribution is unrelated to absorption.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Opposite — that means i is left immediately.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Inconsistent: probabilities wouldn't sum to 1.

medium.prompt: If X and Y are jointly normal with correlation 0, they are…
medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: For jointly normal variables, zero correlation does imply independence (unlike the general case).

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Marginal distributions can differ.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: They are uncorrelated by assumption.

medium.prompt: The law of total expectation says E[X] equals…

choices.label: A
choices.body: E[ E[X | Y] ] for any random variable Y.

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Tower property / iterated expectation; powerful for conditioning arguments.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: That's a worst-case conditional, not the mean.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: That's just E[X] times a probability.

medium.prompt: If X is uniform on [0, 1], what is the distribution of −ln(1 − X) / λ?
medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Inverse-CDF sampling: the inverse CDF of Exponential(λ) is −ln(1 − u) / λ.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Wrong distribution shape.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Bernoulli is discrete.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Not how Gaussian sampling works from uniform.

hard.prompt: Hoeffding's inequality bounds the probability that the sample mean of n bounded i.i.d. variables deviates by more than t as…
hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: For X_i ∈ [a, b], Hoeffding gives exponential concentration in n.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Not Hoeffding's form.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Wrong direction.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: That's an asymptotic order of magnitude, not a bound.

hard.prompt: The strong law of large numbers states that the sample mean of i.i.d. integrable random variables converges to μ…
hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: SLLN gives almost-sure convergence; the weak law gives convergence in probability.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Convergence in distribution is weaker still.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: L² convergence is yet another mode; SLLN is almost-sure.

hard.prompt: A martingale (M_n) with respect to a filtration satisfies E[M_{n+1} | F_n] = …
hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: The defining property of a martingale: the next value is, on average given the past, equal to the current value.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: That's a submartingale with deterministic drift.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Conditional expectation can depend on the path.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: That would make every martingale zero.

hard.prompt: If X is standard normal, then X² has what distribution?
hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: X² with X ~ N(0,1) is χ²_1 by definition; sum of k independent squared normals is χ²_k.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Squaring a normal is not normal.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Probability integral transform applies to F(X), not X².
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Exp(1/2) actually equals χ²_2, not χ²_1.

hard.prompt: An irreducible aperiodic finite-state Markov chain has…

choices.label: B
choices.body: A stationary distribution only for symmetric chains.

choices.label: C
choices.body: A unique stationary distribution to which the chain converges from any starting distribution.

hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: Perron–Frobenius / Markov chain convergence theorem.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Finite irreducible chains always have one.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Symmetry isn't required.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Irreducibility ensures uniqueness.

hard.prompt: The MGF uniqueness theorem says that if two distributions have MGFs equal in some neighborhood of 0, then…

choices.label: A
choices.body: They have the same mean only.

choices.label: D
choices.body: They have the same support only.

hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: MGFs determine distributions when they exist on an open interval around 0.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: MGF carries all moments.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Joint normality is unrelated.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Support equality is weaker than full distribution equality.

hard.prompt: Jensen's inequality for a convex function ϕ states that…
hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: For concave ϕ the inequality reverses; this is why log E ≥ E log under typical use of MLE-related inequalities.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: That's the concave case.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Not a general consequence.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Equality holds only if ϕ is affine or X is degenerate.

hard.prompt: If (X_n) are i.i.d. with mean μ and finite variance σ², the sample variance S²_n is an unbiased estimator of σ² when defined with denominator…
hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: Dividing by n−1 corrects for using X̄ in place of μ (Bessel's correction).

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Divides yields a biased (low) estimator.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Not a standard formula.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Sum of squared deviations isn't a variance.

hard.prompt: If X and Y are jointly distributed and you want to estimate X from Y minimizing MSE, the optimal estimator is…
hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: E[X | Y] is the L²-projection of X onto the σ-algebra of Y; it minimizes mean squared error.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Only optimal if X is independent of Y.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Y need not be on the right scale or even the right variable.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Mode minimizes 0-1 loss, not MSE.

hard.prompt: The Kolmogorov 0-1 law states that…

choices.label: D
choices.body: Tail events of independent sequences have probability 0 or 1.

hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: Useful in establishing 'event happens infinitely often' results for independent sequences.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Garbage statement.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Only tail events.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: True but unrelated to the 0-1 law.

hard.prompt: Convergence in probability implies…
hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: Probability ⇒ distribution; the reverse implications generally don't hold without extra conditions.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Requires UI of powers.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Requires stronger assumptions (e.g., dominated convergence or BC).
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Needs uniform integrability.

hard.prompt: A copula encodes…

choices.label: A
choices.body: The dependence structure between random variables, separated from their marginals.

hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: Sklar's theorem: any joint CDF F decomposes as C(F_X, F_Y) where C is a copula.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Opposite — copulas leave marginals out.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Variance is a marginal property.

hard.prompt: The Metropolis–Hastings algorithm constructs a Markov chain whose stationary distribution is π by…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Always accepting moves that increase π.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Accepting proposed moves with probability min(1, π(y) q(x | y) / (π(x) q(y | x))).

hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: Detailed balance is satisfied by this acceptance rule, even when the proposal q is asymmetric.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: That's hill-climbing; loses ergodicity.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: MH is for when you can't sample π directly.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Randomness is essential.

hard.prompt: Slutsky's theorem says: if X_n → X in distribution and Y_n → c in probability (constant c), then X_n + Y_n converges to…
hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: Slutsky lets you combine a distributional limit with a probability limit cleanly.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Wrong unless c and X are both 0.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: The theorem gives a clean limit.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Not a limit object.

hard.prompt: If X and Y are random variables, then E[XY] − E[X]E[Y] equals…
hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: Definition of covariance.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: That includes variances plus 2 Cov.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Only when X and Y are uncorrelated.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Variance is the covariance of X with itself.

hard.prompt: The Cauchy distribution is notorious because…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Its mean and variance are undefined (the integrals diverge).

choices.label: C
choices.body: It has the largest possible variance.

hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: Heavy tails make moments infinite; the CLT doesn't apply to i.i.d. Cauchy samples.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: F(x) = (1/π) arctan(x − x_0) + 1/2 exists.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Cauchy is continuous.

hard.prompt: If X ~ Normal(μ, σ²), then (X − μ)/σ has…
hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: Standardization centers and scales any normal to Standard Normal.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Cauchy is unrelated.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Squaring it would give χ²_1.

hard.prompt: A sufficient statistic T for a parameter θ is one such that…

choices.label: D
choices.body: P(data | T) does not depend on θ.

hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: Sufficiency captures all information about θ in the data — Fisher–Neyman factorization.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: T is a function of data, not the parameter.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: MLE is one estimator; sufficiency is broader.

hard.prompt: The Borel–Cantelli lemma (first half) says: if Σ P(A_n) < ∞, then…
hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: Convergent sum forces almost-sure finiteness of how often the events happen.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Not what the lemma says.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: That's the second Borel–Cantelli (under independence + divergent sum).

hard.prompt: Detailed balance for a Markov chain with stationary distribution π is…

choices.label: A
choices.body: π_i = π_j for all i, j.

choices.label: B
choices.body: π_i P_{ij} = π_j P_{ji} for all i, j.

choices.label: D
choices.body: P_{ij} = P_{ji} for all i, j.

hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: Reversibility under detailed balance ensures π is stationary; the chain is also called reversible.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Uniform stationarity isn't the same as detailed balance.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Reversible chains can have non-uniform π.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: That's a symmetric P, a special case.
